articles.title: ‘Unlike anything we’ve experienced’: fans swarm San Francisco for BTS star’s art exhibition
articles.summary: K-pop star RM gave a boost to the previously struggling SFMOMA with an exhibition of over 100 pieces from his collection Two years ago, RM of the wildly popular K-pop boyband BTS was serving as a soldier in the South Korean military when he received an offer from América Castillo, a museum curator in San Francisco: would he consider an exhibition of his private art collection? “I loved it,” said RM (real name: Kim Namjoon) at the media preview of RM x SFMOMA: Between You and Me , a new exhibition that opened in San Francisco earlier this month and is co-curated by SFMOMA’s Castillo and Hyoeun Kim. “There aren’t many things that show a person more honestly than a collection they’ve built over a long period of time.” Continue reading...

articles.title: A Course Called Ireland: Bill Murray clearly hated making his new golfing show – but it’s extremely fun to binge
articles.summary: In his rogue new travelogue, the Hollywood star tees off, has drunken pub singalongs – but mostly just proves how tired he is of fame I’m suspicious of travelogues, which often feature celebrities in contrived situations, serving up a sentimental postcard of a place that is tantamount to a lie. I also hate how famous people are inexorably drawn to golf: a boring game historically predicated on a rancid mix of social exclusivity and extensive land ownership. So it was perverse of me to watch a show in which author Tom Coyne drives around Ireland playing various courses with his friend, actor Bill Murray. It’s the perfect intersection of none of my interests.
